more_story: The Thirsty Crow: a crow found a pot with a little water at the bottom. It dropped pebbles in one by one until the water rose, and drank. Moral: where there's a will, there's a way.
The Lion and the Mouse: a lion spared a tiny mouse. Later the lion was caught in a net, and the mouse chewed the ropes to free him. Moral: no act of kindness is ever wasted.
The Tortoise and the Hare: the hare raced ahead, then napped. The slow, steady tortoise kept going and won. Moral: slow and steady wins the race.

The Monkey and the Crocodile: a crocodile wanted the monkey's heart and lied to carry him across the river. The monkey said he'd left his heart in the tree, and escaped. Moral: keep calm and think in danger.
The Ant and the Grasshopper: the ant stored food all summer while the grasshopper sang. In winter the ant was ready and the grasshopper was hungry. Moral: prepare today for tomorrow.
The Boy Who Cried Wolf: a shepherd boy shouted “wolf!” as a joke, again and again. When a wolf really came, nobody believed him. Moral: liars aren't believed even when they tell the truth.
The Fox and the Grapes: a fox couldn't reach some grapes and said they were sour anyway. Moral: it's easy to dislike what we can't have.
The Blue Jackal: a jackal fell into blue dye and pretended to be king of the forest, until he howled with other jackals and was found out. Moral: you can't hide your true self for long.
The Two Goats: two goats met on a narrow bridge and fought, and both fell in the river. Two other goats let one pass first, and both crossed safely. Moral: cooperation beats stubbornness.
